research_claim: Pseudo-labeling improves subscription prediction under severe label scarcity.
support: At 10% labels, F1 increased from 0.503 to 0.571 (Conventional PL).

research_claim: Negative-only pseudo-labeling captures nearly all of the benefit of conventional pseudo-labeling.
The benefit of semi-supervised learning decreases as labeled data availability increases.
support: Approximate F1 gain over supervised RF: 10%=0.069, 20%=0.030, 50%=0.010.

research_claim: Gender is the dominant predictor in the frozen Random Forest.
support: Gender ranked first in grouped permutation importance and SHAP.

research_claim: The predictive dependence on Gender reflects a strong structural characteristic of the dataset.
support: Cramer's V=0.417; F1 decreased by 0.291 when Gender was removed.

research_claim: Gender has a causal effect on subscription.
support: Observational/synthetic data and post-hoc analysis do not establish causality.

research_claim: Cluster-guided pseudo-labeling is the primary source of the semi-supervised improvement.
support: K-Prototypes produced weak separation and cluster guidance was not retained as the primary mechanism.
